public_rationale: Shumer's essay says AI builds apps that are 'usually perfect', done 'with no corrections needed', and that it writes 'hundreds of thousands of lines that work correctly'. Each of these rests on his own experience. The one dataset he cites is METR's task-time measure. It tracks how long a task a model can finish, not whether whole complex apps come out error-free, and he does not mention its 50% success threshold. The essay gives no error rates, studies, or benchmark results on reliable whole-app building. Marcus's description fits the text.
limitations: Shumer's wording is 'usually perfect', slightly weaker than 'without making errors'.
Whether METR counts as relevant 'data' is a matter of reading, but it does not measure error-free app building.
